questions.question: When slowing down, you should ____ to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brakes to slow down. This makes your brake lights flash. Drivers behind you will see the warning.

questions.question: Who is responsible for the safe operation of a vehicle?
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for safe vehicle operation. Check your vehicle before driving.

questions.question: When loading a tank divided by bulkheads with liquid cargo, where should most of the weight go?

options.text: In the top of the tank.
In the middle of the tank.
In the rear of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the middle of the tank.
questions.explanation: Place most weight in the middle of the tank. Do not put too much weight on the front or rear.

questions.question: When should you slow down and be extra careful?
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful in work zones, where the road drops off, when objects are on the road, and on freeway ramps.

questions.question: How much water is needed for a vehicle to hydroplane?

options.text: A good amount, such as a large puddle

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose grip and slide on water. It does not take much water for this to occur.

questions.question: When starting your vehicle, the coolant temperature should:

options.text: Quickly jump from low to high.

questions.explanation: After starting the engine, watch your gauges. The coolant temperature should rise slowly to the normal operating level.

questions.question: When should mirrors be adjusted?
questions.explanation: Check and adjust your mirrors before you start driving.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It allows a vehicle's wheels to lock up.
It prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
It makes turning a vehicle easier.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops your wheels from locking during hard braking. It reduces braking pressure to keep wheels from locking.

questions.question: When are you most likely to encounter strong winds?
questions.explanation: Strong winds can push your vehicle out of its lane. This is especially true when leaving a tunnel.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what happens when the vehicle starts?

options.text: The ABS indicator light should turn on, then quickly shut off.
The steering wheel will not move until the air tanks are full.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS indicator light should turn on, then quickly shut off.
questions.explanation: When you start an ABS-equipped vehicle, the indicator light comes on, then turns off. If the light stays on, the ABS has a problem.

questions.question: When a driver stops and leaves their vehicle carrying hazardous materials, where should the shipping papers be?

options.text: Left in the front seat of the cab.
Placed in a box under the passenger seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left in the front seat of the cab.
questions.explanation: When a driver exits the vehicle, hazardous materials shipping papers must be left on the driver's seat.

questions.question: When filling a tank divided by bulkheads, where should most of the weight be placed?
questions.explanation: When filling a tank divided by bulkheads, distribute weight carefully. Do not put too much weight on the front or rear.

questions.question: Which statement about hydroplaning is true?

options.text: It rarely happens with large trucks.
It usually happens only when traveling faster than 65 mph.
It can happen with only a small amount of water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen with only a small amount of water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose grip and slide on a layer of water. It does not require a large amount of water on the road.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.explanation: Keep liquid discharge valves on a compressed gas tank open during loading and unloading. Close them at all other times.

questions.question: When loading corrosive materials, what should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: When loading corrosive liquids by hand, load containers one at a time. Keep them upright. Never drop or roll the containers.

questions.question: What does pushing in the trailer air supply control do?
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull it out to stop the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve for parking?

options.text: Use it only for parking on a downgrade.

questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can release air pressure and cause the brakes to fail. Use the parking brake or wheel chocks instead.

questions.question: What will CDL applicants be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?
questions.explanation: The vehicle inspection test includes checking the oil level. You must show that it is safe for operation.

questions.question: What mainly determines your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: BAC is mainly determined by how much alcohol you consume, how fast you drink it, and your body weight.

questions.question: For which offense will a CDL be disqualified?

options.text: Two convictions for using a hand-held mobile phone while driving.
A driver listening to the radio too loudly.
Turning right at a red stoplight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two convictions for using a hand-held mobile phone while driving.
questions.explanation: A CDL will be disqualified after two or more convictions for using a hand-held mobile phone while operating a commercial vehicle.
